one_liner: Explain and tune vLLM's PagedAttention block manager, scheduler, prefix caching, and multi-LoRA internals.

key_terms.definition: System and kernel that pages the KV cache into fixed-size blocks mapped via per-sequence block tables, eliminating fragmentation and enabling sharing.
Stored per-layer key and value vectors for every generated token, read on each decode step instead of being recomputed.
Fixed-size chunk of KV-cache token-slots (commonly 16 tokens) that is the unit of allocation and sharing in PagedAttention.
Per-sequence ordered mapping from logical block index to physical block ID, letting a sequence's KV cache live in non-contiguous memory.
vLLM's refcounted allocator that owns the pool of physical KV blocks, handing them to sequences and reclaiming them on release.
Iteration-level scheduling where requests join or leave the running batch at token granularity instead of waiting for a whole batch to finish.
Splitting a long prompt's prefill into token-budget-sized chunks interleaved with other requests' decode steps within the same forward pass.
When a shared KV block needs to be written, allocate a fresh block and copy contents into it rather than clobbering the shared original.
Reusing previously computed KV blocks of a matching prompt prefix, identified via rolling block hashes, instead of recomputing them.
A cheap drafter proposes several future tokens, verified in one target-model forward pass via rejection sampling that preserves the exact output distribution.
Serving many low-rank adapters on one shared base model by computing each request's adapter contribution as a batched, gathered low-rank matmul.
A recorded, replayable sequence of GPU kernel launches captured for a fixed batch shape, cutting per-step CPU launch overhead during decode.

prerequisites: prefill and decode in autoregressive inference
GPU memory hierarchy and kernel launch overhead
